sites.name: Apollo 11
sites.description: The first crewed landing on the Moon. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin explored the lunar surface while Michael Collins orbited above.

sites.name: Apollo 17
sites.description: The final crewed Apollo landing brought a geologist to the Moon and returned a rich collection of samples from the valley.

sites.name: Chang’e 4
sites.description: The first successful soft landing on the Moon’s far side. The lander and Yutu-2 rover explored the South Pole–Aitken basin.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3
sites.description: India’s Vikram lander and Pragyan rover reached the lunar south polar region and carried out a short surface science campaign.

sites.name: Artemis south polar region
sites.description: NASA’s Artemis campaign is preparing for future crewed exploration near the lunar south pole. This marker is illustrative; a landing site has not been selected.

mars.label: Mars
mars.caption: Viking MDIM21 global color mosaic · NASA Trek

sites.name: Perseverance
sites.description: NASA’s rover is exploring an ancient lake-and-delta environment, collecting rock cores, and searching for signs of past microbial life.

sites.name: Curiosity
sites.description: Curiosity studies Mount Sharp and the chemistry of ancient Martian environments that could once have supported microbial life.

sites.name: Viking 1
sites.description: Viking 1 was the first spacecraft to return successful images from the surface of Mars and performed the first U.S. Mars landing.

sites.name: Viking 2
sites.description: Viking 2 paired orbital reconnaissance with a lander that returned surface images and atmospheric and soil measurements.

sites.name: InSight
sites.description: The stationary lander studied Mars’ interior, measured marsquakes, and helped reveal the planet’s crust, mantle, and core.

sites.name: Opportunity
sites.description: Built for a 90-sol mission, Opportunity explored Meridiani Planum for nearly 15 years and found evidence of ancient water.
